title: Audit Operations Lead
description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role You will run the external audit calendar for our SOX 404 program as we scale toward an IPO. That means coordinating with our external auditors across the year, aligning testing windows with control owners, educating our control owners, and keeping requests and deliverables on schedule. You will also own SOX scoping and risk assessment cycles, deficiency tracking, and status reporting, and help roll out our GRC platform so the program runs from one system of record instead of spreadsheets. You will scale the program through AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual effort and speed up our SOX program. This role reports to the Head of Business Controls and works closely with everyone on the SOX and Internal Audit team. This is an individual contributor role for someone who keeps a complex program on schedule, writes clearly, and makes the program simpler each cycle. Key responsibilities Own the annual SOX audit calendar, including interim and year-end testing windows, walkthrough schedules, and key deliverable dates agreed with external auditors. Serve as the day-to-day point of contact for external auditor requests. Triage, route, and track each request to closure, including PBC (provided-by-client) lists and evidence deliveries. Coordinate auditor walkthroughs and fieldwork with process owners, control owners, and the SOX Testing team, so each control owner is asked for the same evidence once. Track auditor findings, management responses, and deficiency follow-ups, and report status to Internal Audit leadership. Prepare control owners and process owners for auditor sessions, and get evidence delivered on time without direct authority over them. Lead the annual SOX scoping and risk assessment, including quarterly refreshes, and support the annual Fraud Risk Assessment, so the program has appropriate scope and coverage under COSO. Monitor BP and IT SOX testing and report status to leadership and share status with external auditors Lead work with the business to improve control documentation, including education of templates and SOX guidance. Find optimization and automation opportunities across the SOX lifecycle through the use of AI. Support the rollout of the GRC tool for SOX, including control libraries, workflows, evidence requests, and testing templates. Define the data and reporting requirements the platform must meet, and test that it produces what the program needs. Run the quarterly sub-certification process and report results to leadership Own SOX program status reporting: dashboards and metrics for leadership, audit calendar progress, and deficiency and remediation status. Own status reporting for the full SOX lifecycle: scoping and risk assessment, testing, deficiencies and remediation, segregation of duties (SOD), SOC 1 report reviews, the fraud risk assessment, and audit calendar progress. Minimum qualifications Big 4 audit firm experience on SOX 404 or ICFR engagements, including managing audit calendars, PBC requests, and fieldwork with external audit teams. Experience working directly with external auditor teams on requests, testing schedules, and findings, from the company side. Several years of hands-on SOX 404 experience, including scoping, risk assessment, control documentation, testing, and deficiency evaluation. Working knowledge of the COSO framework, ICFR, and PCAOB standards. Experience developing or maintaining Risk and Control Matrices and process documentation or flowcharts. Experience implementing or administering a GRC systems Experience reporting program status, metrics, and issues to senior leadership. Ability to get control owners to deliver on time without authority over them. Clear writing and calm coordination under deadline pressure. A Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent experience. Preferred qualifications In-house SOX experience at a pre-IPO or newly public company. Experience running a fraud risk assessment. CPA, CISA, or similar certification. Comfort with SQL or data tools for reporting, and experience building lightweight automations, including with Claude. title: Internal Audit Operations Lead Associate
description: Playing an essential role in the U.S. economy, Fannie Mae is foundational to housing finance. Here, your expertise can help fuel purpose-driven innovation that expands access to homeownership and affordable rental housing across the country. Join Fannie Mae to grow your career and help people find a place to call home. Job Description As a valued colleague on our Internal Audit Operations audit team, you will be responsible for leading and executing risk-based internal audits to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls, risk management practices, and governance processes across the organization. This role provides oversight throughout the audit lifecycle, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements, corporate policies, and industry standards while identifying opportunities to strengthen operational efficiency and mitigate risks. THE IMPACT YOU WILL MAKE The Internal Audit Operations Lead Associate role will offer you the flexibility to make each day your own, while working alongside people who care so that you can deliver on the following responsibilities: Audit Planning and Execution: Lead end-to-end audit engagements, including risk assessments, audit planning, control testing, documentation, and reporting. Risk and Control Assessment: Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of internal controls, identify control deficiencies, and recommend corrective actions. Team Leadership: Supervise and mentor audit team members, review workpapers, and ensure audit engagements meet quality standards and deadlines. Regulatory Compliance: Assess adherence to applicable regulatory requirements, internal policies, and established risk management frameworks. Stakeholder Management: Collaborate with business leaders, risk management teams, and senior management to communicate audit findings and recommendations. THE EXPERIENCE YOU BRING TO THE TEAM Minimum Required Experiences and Skills 4 years of audit experience. Knowledge of the audit life cycle, including planning, design assessment, operating effectiveness testing, reporting, and issue monitoring. Prior experience leading a team of auditors and reviewing audit materials. Strong critical thinking and analytical skills to evaluate risks, controls, business processes, and data sets. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly document and share audit results. Ability to collaborate effectively with business partners, audit team members, and management. Shows curiosity and adaptability in learning and responsibly applying new technologies, including artificial intelligence, to reimagine how we work. Desired Experience Bachelor’s degree or equivalent. Audit experience within the financial services or mortgage industry is highly desired. CIA, CPA, CISA certification preferred or in the processes of obtaining. The ideal candidate will possess a combination of technical expertise, software development experience, cybersecurity and compliance knowledge, and the ability to translate complex business requirements into scalable AI-driven solutions. Experience within highly regulated industries, particularly financial services, is strongly preferred. Design and maintain complex integrations between governance platforms, compliance systems, security tooling, data repositories, and reporting solutions. title: ETF and 1940 Act Registered Funds Compliance Officer - Vice President
description: About the Role iCapital is looking to hire a Compliance Officer to help oversee the relevant investment advisers supporting the Exchange-Traded Funds (ETF), Alternative Investments Fund-of-Funds and 1940 Act Registered Funds businesses. This individual will also be responsible for assisting the implementation and administration of compliance programs for the firm’s SEC Registered Investment Advisers, Investment Company Act, NFA and CFTC registered Commodity Pools, and other compliance-related activities as they relate to these products or entities.   Responsibilities Maintain expert knowledge of regulations applicable to ETFs and 1940 Act Registered Funds and their investment advisers, including the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, Investment Company Act of 1940, and Rule 6c‑11. Oversee the administration of the Fund's compliance and governance framework.   Assist in monitoring compliance with fund governing documents. Advise on regulatory developments affecting ETFs, including derivatives, valuation, liquidity, and related rulemaking.  Provide compliance leadership and support for ETF and Registered Funds initiatives, including identifying regulatory risks and developing practical solutions.  Advise Product, Portfolio Management, Operations, and other stakeholders on product structuring, operations, investment strategies, and disclosures.  Review fund marketing materials for consistency with fund disclosures, governing documents, regulatory requirements, and internal policies, and coordinate approvals with relevant stakeholders.  Translate regulatory requirements and fund governing documents into scalable policies, procedures, and compliance controls.  Oversee product‑specific compliance obligations, including disclosure monitoring, premium or discount reporting, and regulatory filings.  Conduct post‑trade compliance monitoring, portfolio guideline testing, and issue resolution.  Support trading oversight frameworks, including best execution governance and related compliance practices.  Perform compliance testing, reporting, and remediation tracking to ensure timely resolution of issues.  Oversee and coordinate compliance reviews of third‑party service providers, including administrators, custodians, legal counsel, and auditors.  Qualifications Bachelor’s degree is required; Law Degree or MBA is preferred  10+ years of compliance experience in the financial services industry, including a robust understanding of and experience with exchange-traded funds, derivatives, alternatives and the regulatory landscape  Demonstrated knowledge of U.S. securities laws, particularly the Investment Company Act of 1940, the Investment Advisers Act of 1040, the Securities Act of 1933, the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and other SEC, CFTC, NFA and FINRA regulations  Strong knowledge and prior experience with investment company, investment adviser, and NFA or CFTC compliance programs and requirements  Strong experience in dealing with matters associated with Rule 38a-1 under the Investment Company Act of 1940 and Rule 206(4)-7 under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940  Experience with regulatory examinations, investigations or other interactions specifically with the SEC, FINRA and NFA  Experience evaluating risk and mapping risk and controls across firm practices  Skilled at developing other team members through mentoring or helping upskill  Able to operate in a fast-paced environment  Detail oriented with the ability to assess and prioritize projects  FINRA Series 7 and 24 licenses are preferred    Benefits The base salary range for this role is $150,000 to $180,000. iCapital offers a compensation package which includes salary, equity for all full-time employees, and an annual performance bonus. Employees also receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes an employer matched retirement plan, generously subsidized healthcare with 100% employer paid dental, vision, telemedicine, and virtual mental health counseling, parental leave, and unlimited paid time off (PTO). We believe the best ideas and innovation happen when we are together. Employees in this role will work in the office Monday-Thursday, with the flexibility to work remotely on Friday. title: Governance Lead, Scheme Compliance

At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition.  For our teams, we create an environment with opportunities for our people to succeed, backed by the culture and support to ensure they are enabled to truly own their careers. We are motivated individuals who tackle unique technical challenges at scale and solve them as a team. Together, we deliver innovative and ethical solutions that help businesses achieve their ambitions faster.  About the role We are looking for a strategic, structured, and collaborative leader to lead the Governance pillar within Adyen’s global Scheme Compliance team. You will manage a small globally distributed team, setting the direction for how we demonstrate compliance with card scheme and local payment method requirements through effective governance, control assurance, and coordinated external engagement. This role combines people leadership with accountability for our global governance framework, audit and assessment coordination, internal control mapping and testing, and relationships with scheme Risk and Compliance counterparts. Manage, coach, and develop team members across regions, establishing clear responsibilities, priorities, and development opportunities. Balance planned assurance work with incoming scheme requests and emerging priorities. Own the governance framework. Define and maintain consistent standards for scheme, debit network, and alternative payment method compliance documentation, control mapping, evidence management, issue tracking, and reporting across the program pillars. Lead audit and assessment coordination. Oversee Scheme Compliance’s participation in scheme and local payment method audits, assessments, and due diligence reviews. Coordinate scope, subject-matter contributions, evidence, responses, and follow-up with accountable stakeholders. Oversee control mapping and testing. Lead the mapping of scheme and payment method requirements to internal policies and controls. Establish a risk-based testing plan with Internal Controls and pillar leads, ensuring control gaps are documented, assessed, and escalated. Serve as the global governance point of contact. Act as the central interface for scheme Risk and Compliance counterparts, connecting the appropriate regional and subject-matter owners while maintaining a consistent global approach. Manage scheme communications and RFIs. Oversee the intake, routing, coordination, and quality review of scheme and local payment method communications and requests for information. Ensure responses are accurate, consistent, appropriately reviewed, and delivered on time. Lead recurring scheme governance engagements. Own the preparation and coordination of weekly business reviews (WBRs), quarterly business reviews (QBRs), and annual meetings, including agendas, reporting, stakeholder preparation, and tracking of decisions and commitments. Partner on assurance and remediation. Work closely with Internal Audit and Internal Controls to align assurance activities, support independent reviews, and reduce unnecessary duplication. Challenge remediation plans, monitor progress, and escalate overdue actions or unresolved risks. Own committee and board reporting. Lead the preparation, consolidation, and delivery of Scheme Compliance reporting to committees, boards, and management forums across all regions and management levels. Ensure reporting provides a clear, consistent view of compliance risks, control effectiveness, audit findings, remediation progress, and scheme commitments, with appropriate escalation of matters requiring attention or decisions. Own the global scheme bulletin intake and update process. Oversee the intake, tracking, distribution, and status reporting of bulletins and rule updates from all schemes globally. Ensure relevant owners assess applicability and impact, establish required actions and deadlines, and provide evidence of completion. Maintain a consolidated view of progress and escalate gaps, delays, or unresolved ownership. title: Sanctions Compliance Lead
description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's Integrity & Compliance (I&C) function is building the systems that let us scale responsibly as our products reach more people, more enterprises, and more regulated industries. Our global compliance program is bespoke, reflecting our unique mission and position as one of the leading AI labs operating on the frontier. Our Regulatory Programs pillar is a key pillar of our overall Integrity & Compliance function and covers a range of compliance domain areas including economic sanctions, US export controls, and regulatory compliance programs stemming from global content and AI regulation. As Sanctions Compliance Lead, you will take day-to-day leadership of Anthropic's sanctions compliance program and support oversight of our export controls program, supporting the Regulatory Programs lead as a senior leader within the function. This is a leadership seat in a domain where the rules governing AI models and compute are still being written, and where sanctions exposure runs through globally accessible APIs, downstream and embedded-partner channels, and rapid geographic expansion. You will own the sanctions program end to end: setting strategy and risk appetite with leadership, continuously assessing risk and driving remediation and program enhancements, governing our screening and enforcement controls, directing regulator-facing matters, and reporting on program health to I&C leadership and the Audit Committee. You will partner closely with our in-house Trade Compliance Counsel on interpretation of applicable law, represent the function with senior stakeholders, and lead and develop trade compliance professionals as the team grows. This is a builder's role at a company that takes integrity seriously and moves fast. You will exercise independent judgment on issues without clear precedent and build durable programs that let Anthropic move quickly while honoring its obligations to regulators, customers, and the public.
